findings.title: Generalized keyword-name resolution fixes OwlViT semantic input bindings without recipe reordering
findings.observation: At google/owlvit-base-patch16 revision 4b420debb9c806fc4caf9ecc8efb72208c0db892 with WinML 0.2.0, Transformers 4.57.6, Torch 2.13.0, ONNX Runtime 1.27.0, and CPUExecutionProvider, the vendor OwlViTOnnxConfig emitted pixel_values before input_ids while OwlViTForObjectDetection.forward accepts input_ids before pixel_values. Keyword invocation exported successfully, but current main attached pixel_values to INT32[1,16] and input_ids to FLOAT[1,3,768,768]. Resolving ONNX input_names from the complete forward signature corrected the semantic bindings in recipe-free, fp32, and fp16 builds. The final fp32/fp16 graphs had 1025/1030 nodes and 28 operator types; dominant fp32 operators were Reshape 411, Gemm 150, and Transpose 121. Public-rule analysis found no partial or unsupported operator types, while Einsum plus some Cast/Sqrt signatures remained unknown on rule-backed EPs. Export metadata reported 152,789,511 parameters, 319 modules, and 106 traced modules, rooted at OwlViTForObjectDetection → OwlViTModel → vision/text towers plus class and box heads. Autoconf expanded optim from {} to gelu_fusion=true and matmul_add_fusion=true.
findings.effort_tier_required: L0 on current main; the historical generalized exporter repair was L1
gotchas: Do not infer semantic correctness from export success: verify every ONNX input name against its real shape and dtype.
Do not reorder keyword-invoked recipe inputs solely to match forward(); current main resolves keyword names from the complete signature. Preserve explicit positional get_export_args protocols.
Preserve explicit get_export_args positional protocols instead of reordering them by forward signature.
CPU fp16 conversion halves external weights (609,623,040 to 304,811,008 bytes) but was slower than fp32 in this host measurement.
winml eval has no zero-shot-object-detection task, so L3 is CLI-BLOCKED.
feature_gaps_filed: https://github.com/microsoft/winml-cli/issues/1147 — add zero-shot-object-detection schema and evaluator to winml eval
findings.mechanism_notes: Regression tests prove the keyword-name resolver follows inspect.signature(model.forward) only on a complete unambiguous match and preserves model-defined get_export_args ordering. Recipe-free and both precision builds proved corrected named bindings.
